messages:
alex: Heads up — ran into a failure in the embeddings batch helper while paginating a ~150k-row dataset. Error: 'expected dim 1536 got 768' during rerank pipeline. Anyone seen this before?
matt: which SDK / language?
alex: python sdk 0.9.2 for the batcher step, but the rerank part calls our Go client. The batch helper is our internal util that assembles pages into big numpy arrays.
jen: first guess: mixed models. 1536 vs 768 screams large vs base embedding model mismatch.
alex: I thought we pinned model via config to "open-embedding-large" but unit tests locally were passing. Strange.
liam: also check if you're concatenating streaming responses incorrectly — streaming can yield item chunks that, if concatenated wrong, might double up dims.
shreya: can you paste the snippet where you assemble the embeddings?
alex: snippet:
```python
emb = client.embeddings.create(model="open-embedding-large", input=batch)
# we then do np.vstack([e.data[0].embedding for e in emb])
```
matt: in the Python SDK the response is a dict-like structure. Typical pattern is `resp['data'][i]['embedding']`. That indexing looks off for the SDK shape you expect.
alex: hmm, true — that line is from an older wrapper we use. But I still suspect something else because some items return 1536 and some 768.
jen: any quantization / post-processing step between call and assembly? e.g., a goroutine doing float16 conversion?
alex: not intentionally. no quantize path.
devex-bot: FYI — there's an open issue #432 about cursor off-by-one when using page_size=1000 that caused mixed page sizes for a while.
matt: pagination gotchas: our list endpoint returns {items, next_cursor}. next_cursor == "" (empty string) when finished. If your loop uses `while cursor:` you'll break early for empty string — but that causes missing rows, not dim mismatch.
alex: good call though — our loop uses `while cursor is not None` in Go but `while cursor:` in py. I'll audit that.
shreya: another angle — are both SDKs explicitly setting model param? If Go client fallback defaults to a smaller model, you'll get mixed dims when assembling across services. Check REDWOOD_MODEL or ~/.redwood/config defaults.
alex: digging now — confirmed: our Go call path didn't set model (relied on server default). Staging cluster default was recently changed to "open-embed-small" (768). So Python was requesting large, Go used default small.
liam: nice catch. Two action items: 1) patch our Go client callsite to pass explicit model from config; 2) hard assert in the batcher that all embeddings have identical dims before np.vstack and fail fast with helpful msg.
jen: and add a unit test that simulates mixed-model responses so this doesn't regress.
alex: will do a small PR with both fixes + test. pinging @matt for review when ready.
matt: I can review. Also add a telemetry metric `embedding_dim_mismatch` so we can alert if this happens in prod.
alex: added to TODO list. Quick question re: streaming semantics — for embeddings, does streaming ever return partial vectors?
matt: for generation streaming yields tokens. For embeddings, our current streaming mode emits full embeddings per item (no partial vectors). If you see partial-length vectors it's a bug (or a different model).
alex: thanks — that narrows it.
jen: small implementation note: when assembling from pages, prefer `np.concatenate([arrs], axis=0)` with a dtype check first — avoids implicit casts.
shreya: also ensure your batcher normalizes model ids (lowercase / canonical) since we had a recent bug where "Open-Embedding-Large" and "open-embedding-large" were treated as different keys in our cache.
alex: good call. I'll normalize. PR ETA ~30m.
matt: :thumbsup:
jen: :shipit:
alex: PR: 1779246 — fixes model selection in Go path, adds assert on dims, pagination cursor fix in py, and a unit test that simulates mixed dims.
matt: reviewing now.
ci-bot: build passed for PR/1779246 — all tests green.
matt: approved, merging.
ci-bot: merge complete. Deploy triggered.
devops: heads up — canary to staging rolling. We may see higher memory while large batches land. Please monitor `staging-embeddings` pod mem.
alex: will monitor logs and metrics. Thanks everyone — will follow up if anything odd pops up.
